issues.source_quote: Здравствуйте... - Здравствуйте. - Э... скажите, пожалуйста, Ваше имя-отчество...
issues.translation_quote: Hello... - Hello. - Uh... tell me, please, your name and patronymic...
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the fixed Soviet joke 'Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица' and 'Аптека Чиканук' phrasing is rendered as 'Fries Street, Fish Street', losing the deliberate broken-language spy-code feel; 'Fries' misleads (fries/chips) and 'Fish Street' is not the intended 'Fish Street' garbled.

issues.source_quote: Мы вообще дальше Дубровки никуда не ездили.
issues.translation_quote: We've never even been further than Dubrovka.
issues.justification: Dubrovka is a culturally specific place (a small nearby locale) and the joke about provincial limits is unexplained; minor loss, but the later 'in Dubrovka' lines depend on it.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш любимый шеф, если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: As our beloved boss says: 'If a man is an idiot, it's for a long time!'
issues.justification: Literal rendering kills the punchline; the natural English echo is 'once an idiot, always an idiot' / 'being an idiot is a lifelong condition'. The recurring boss-aphorism gag is flattened.

issues.source_quote: Лёлик, я не понимаю, о чем ты говоришь? Сейчас поймёшь! К шефу! Только без рук!
issues.justification: 'Только без рук' here means 'no rough stuff / keep your hands to yourself' but Lyolik is threatening; more importantly later 'Лёлик только без рук' is rendered identically, losing the comic sense of Gesha begging not to be hit.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a whole ticket pack, win... a tractor rack!
issues.justification: The rhyming jingle is mistranslated: 'водокачку' is a water pump tower (an absurd prize); 'tractor rack' is invented and the comic absurdity of the lottery prize is lost.

issues.source_quote: за чужой счёт пьют даже трезвенники и язвенники
issues.justification: 'Язвенники' means people with stomach ulcers, not convalescents; the punchline (even ulcer sufferers drink free booze) is mistranslated.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! May I see you in a coffin, in white slippers! May you live... on nothing but... your salary!
issues.justification: The curse's comic non-standard speech ('у гробу, у белых тапках') is lost, and the hesitant ellipses in the last curse are inserted, weakening the comic escalation; register of a Soviet curse is flattened.

issues.source_quote: Собака - друг человека! ... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: The building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: Acceptable literal rendering, but the later leitmotif is fine; however 'Управдом' as 'building manager' loses the bureaucratic Soviet flavour (house manager/housing committee chair).

issues.source_quote: Пьянству - бой!
issues.justification: Soviet slogan rendered adequately, but 'Тлетворное влияние Запада' etc. fine; main issue is elsewhere. (Low confidence.)

issues.source_quote: Измена
issues.justification: Nadya says 'В измене!' meaning infidelity/betrayal (she suspects an affair and recruitment); 'treason' narrows it to political betrayal and removes the ambiguity driving the joke.

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's hot, without leaving the till!
issues.justification: The boss's mangled-idiom catchphrase (mixing two proverbs) is translated literally with an odd hybrid; acceptable and consistent, but 'without leaving the till' is stilted.

issues.source_quote: Ха-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га-га!
issues.justification: Extremely long transliterated laugh strings are repeated rather than conveyed as subtitle-friendly [laughs]; clutters reading.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No! I ain't doing no such thing!
issues.justification: Lyolik is imitating a rustic/plebeian cabbie voice for comic effect, but the rendering is a heavy American dialect ('ain't ... no such') that mismatches the Soviet setting.

issues.source_quote: Угу... С чьего трупа?
issues.justification: Fine overall; but 'Но человека можно... напоить' is rendered 'a person can be... gotten drunk' which is ungrammatical and awkward.

issues.source_quote: Я боюсь... Боюсь, смогу ли я, способен ли?
issues.justification: Source says he's unsure whether he is capable; 'overpowered by fear' is an addition that changes the nuance and sounds unnatural.

issues.source_quote: Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица
issues.justification: Garbled, accented spy-code phrase is turned into a plausible-sounding street name with an unrelated 'Fries'; the intentional nonsense code is lost.

issues.source_quote: Пора, турыст! Нынадо... Иди...
issues.translation_quote: Time to go, toorist! Dun't... Go...
issues.justification: Eye-dialect spellings are inconsistent and unclear; the speaker's meaning ('Нельзя/не надо') is obscured.

issues.source_quote: Добрый день! Бонжур, мадам... - Пардон.
issues.translation_quote: Salut, boy! I'm from the boss.
issues.justification: Fine; but 'Ксива? Паспорт... готов! Хаза?' rendered as 'Crib?' is American slang, off-register for criminal slang of the era.

issues.source_quote: Двухкоечный нумер
issues.justification: The invented spelling 'rhoom' does not convey the Russian mispronunciation/archaism and looks like a typo.

issues.source_quote: Печёнкой чую, клюнула настоящая рыба.
issues.translation_quote: I can feel it in my gut, a real fish has bitten.
issues.justification: 'Печёнкой' (liver) idiom flattened; 'bitten' for fish biting is unnatural ('taken the bait').

issues.source_quote: Вы ко мне приедете. Если мы Вам будем нужны… Я вызываю такси на своё имя.
issues.translation_quote: If we need you... You'll come to me. If you need us... I call a taxi in my own name.
issues.justification: Roles are garbled: the Russian has Mikhail Ivanych saying that if he needs Semyon, Semyon's called; if Semyon needs them, Semyon orders a taxi in his own name. The translation reverses who calls the taxi, confusing the plot mechanism.

issues.source_quote: Каким приятелем? Ну, с тем, с которым Вы были... на рыбалке, в ресторане…
issues.justification: Semyon asks why they didn't arrest Gena then ('почему же вы его тогда не...'); 'Then' is vague and loses the point that Gena is already suspected.

issues.source_quote: Ясно - собутыльник! Ну-ка иди отсюда, Миша! Как у вас там говорят, топай до хазы.
issues.translation_quote: As your lot say, beat it back to your crib.
issues.justification: The comic jab at criminal slang is rendered with American 'crib', anachronistic for a Soviet film.

issues.source_quote: Мне бы пивка…
issues.justification: 'Тогда я тебя укушу' is a drunken-insistence gag; rendering is acceptable but 'Bite! Grr...' loses the humor of Semyon's comic compliance.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, нет такого мужа, который, хоть на час бы не мечтал стать холостяком!
issues.translation_quote: there's no husband who hasn't dreamed, if only for an hour, of being a bachelor!
issues.justification: Acceptable; however, the preceding 'Следить за сигналом' etc. fine. (Low confidence.)

issues.source_quote: Неужели ты ничего не помнишь? - Осторожно! - Осторожнас...
issues.justification: Gesha's mock-foreign 'Осторожнас' is an intentional comic mispronunciation; 'Carefuls' is meaningless in English.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: Such is "c'est la vie", as they say over there...
issues.justification: The Russian deliberately mangles the phrase ('такова сё ля ви'); correct French spelling erases the joke.

issues.source_quote: Не-к... А кока-колу пил? ... К-к... [фигня]
issues.justification: Bracketed gloss 'rubbish' is British register and odd; Semyon's dismissal of Coca-Cola would be fine as 'Yuck'.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.justification: 'Twasn't' is archaic/poetic register that does not fit Anna's modern voice.

issues.source_quote: Зубы заговаривает...
issues.justification: Idiom meaning 'he's talking me around' translated blandly.

issues.source_quote: Ах, он такой доверчивый...
issues.justification: Fine.
